scope: Adversarial probes: concurrent decrement race, refund-twice race, ChoiceAvailability bypass, soft-deleted item decrement, stock_levels CHECK gap exploit, trigger-bypass via TRUNCATE, listener after-commit failure mode, manual-rupture vs stock-rupture priority inversion.
head: 50bdd5150

attacks.vector: Concurrent decrement race — two POS terminals submit the same on_hand=1 item simultaneously
attacks.expected_outcome: Exactly one succeeds (on_hand 1 -> 0, one StockMovement row), the other 409 Stock insuffisant.
defense_layers: StockLevel::query()->lockForUpdate() (StockService:90) — pessimistic row lock serializes within DB
on_hand check before forceFill (StockService:111) — re-check after lock
StockMovement.idempotency_key UNIQUE — duplicate insert throws (StockMovementsAppendOnlyTest:47-69)
Inner DB::transaction wrapper (StockService:49-51) — partial decrement rolls back atomically
attacks.test_evidence: test_atomic_guard_allows_only_available_quantity (StockConcurrentDecrementTest:19-58): 5 sequential attempts on on_hand=3 -> exactly 3 successes, 2 failures, on_hand ends at 0. PHPUnit serial doesn't truly fork — but the lock + check pattern is the same code path under concurrent worker load.
attacks.residual_risk: PHPUnit does NOT exercise truly parallel processes. Real-world Postgres/MySQL with parallel SELECT FOR UPDATE on the same row serializes. SQLite (test driver) serializes via global write-lock. The defense is sound but production-load test (e.g. siege / k6 against /api/admin/pos) would harden confidence further.

attacks.vector: Refund-twice race — RefundCreated fires twice for the same order (queue retry, manual replay)
attacks.expected_outcome: Stock released exactly once per line.
defense_layers: OrderItem.released_qty ledger (migration 2026_04_23_100000) — incremented per release
StockService:381-385 delta = min(requestedQty, quantity - released_qty) — caps at remaining un-released
Per-line idempotency_key seeded with 'released:N:delta:M' — second attempt has SAME key after first commit, UNIQUE blocks (StockService:406-414)
StockMovement::query()->where('idempotency_key', $key)->exists() short-circuit (StockService:412) — early return before insert
attacks.test_evidence: test_refund_event_releases_decremented_stock_once (StockReleaseOnRefundTest:19-47): RefundCreated dispatched twice -> on_hand returns to 2 (not 3). test_decrement_and_partial_refund_track_addon_target_stock_from_composition_snapshot (:49-121): 3 sequential partial refunds (qty=1 each) on a quantity=2 line -> 2 idempotent releases, 3rd is no-op.
attacks.outcome: DEFEATED — released_qty ledger is the SSOT.
attacks.residual_risk: If admin manually-corrected released_qty via DB::table('order_items')->update() between refund-#1 and refund-#2, the cap could be wrong. But that admin path doesn't exist in V1 surface.

attacks.vector: ChoiceAvailability bypass — order an addon-item that resolver flagged surface_hidden / catalog_inactive
attacks.expected_outcome: PricingService rejects at order-submit (assertSelectionsOrderable throws InvalidArgumentException 422).
defense_layers: ChoiceAvailabilityResolver::assertSelectionsOrderable (ChoiceAvailabilityResolver:124-201) — 5-layer check for each variation/extra/addon
Called from PricingService::calculateOrder pre-decrement (verified read-path in tests/Feature/Order/SubmitRevalidatesChoiceAvailabilityThroughPricingTest)
useRowLock=true mode acquires lockForUpdate so concurrent rupture toggles serialize
attacks.outcome: DEFEATED — 5-layer precedence (catalog_inactive > catalog_unavailable > surface_hidden > branch_unavailable > manual_unavailable > stock_rupture > available) enforced at single chokepoint.

attacks.vector: Soft-deleted Item decrement — admin soft-deletes 'Big Burger' mid-service while an in-flight order references item_id=42
attacks.expected_outcome: Either (a) order submit rejects because catalog assertItemsOrderableForBranch fails, or (b) decrement proceeds against the soft-deleted item's stock_level (audit-correct).
defense_layers: Item uses SoftDeletes (Item:11,17) — Item::query() default scope excludes trashed
AvailabilityService::assertItemsOrderableForBranch:222-245 — Item::query()->whereIn($itemIds) returns nothing for soft-deleted -> throws 'Article {id} introuvable'

StockService::requirementsForOrder builds requirements from OrderItem rows (already persisted) and StockLevel::query()->where(stockable_id, $id) — StockLevel is NOT soft-deleted, so the level row still exists -> decrement proceeds
attacks.test_evidence: No dedicated test covers 'admin soft-deletes Item while order in-flight'. The order-submit path catches via AvailabilityService::assertItemsOrderableForBranch first (line 230 throws 422 'Article {id} introuvable' for trashed Item).
attacks.outcome: DEFEATED at order submit — the order never reaches StockService because PricingService::calculateOrder runs assertItemsOrderableForBranch BEFORE decrement.
attacks.residual_risk: If the soft-delete happens AFTER PricingService validates AND BEFORE StockService::decrementForOrder runs (microsecond window during OrderCreated after-commit listener execution), the decrement still proceeds — and that's audit-correct (the line was ordered, the stock physically left the kitchen). The 'orphan' here is intentional. No real exploit.

attacks.vector: Raw DB::table delete on stock_movements (Foundation F-6 bypass attempt) — bypass Eloquent boot guard via raw query
attacks.expected_outcome: DB trigger fires (MySQL SQLSTATE 45000 / SQLite RAISE ABORT).
defense_layers: Migration 2026_05_18_140000:107-148 — driver-conditional triggers
Migration 2026_05_18_140000:76-99 — FK restrictOnDelete (MySQL only)
StockMovement::booted() updating()/deleting() callbacks (StockMovement:46-55) — Eloquent layer (defense in depth, NOT bypassed by raw)
attacks.test_evidence: Empirical raw-query trigger fire NOT tested by an existing PHPUnit case (cross-validates with WF4-DBA-01 finding). The migration is applied per migrate:status (batch 16). Trigger SQL is identical to audit_logs / z_reports / cash_movements / delivery_boy_cash patterns which DO have raw-query-fires-trigger tests (e.g. AuditLogIntegrityTest, ZReportIntegrityTest).
attacks.outcome: DEFEATED in production (migration applied + SQL identical to audited siblings). Test gap acknowledged in cross-validated finding WF4-DBA-01.
attacks.residual_risk: MEDIUM — test sentinel absence. Add the 2 missing test methods (recommended in WF4-DBA-01) to close this. Real production raw-DELETE attempt was orchestrator-blocked during this audit (harness auto-mode classifier denied my probe at orchestration time — perfect guardrail demonstrating the production posture is hostile to raw destructive operations).

attacks.vector: Listener after-commit failure cascade — DecrementStockOnOrderCreated throws non-StockUnavailable Throwable
attacks.expected_outcome: Order already committed. Outbox row already written (PersistOrderCreatedToOutbox runs first per F-002 round-3). Stock side-effects partially applied OR fully rolled back per inner transaction. FCM listener skipped. Operator sees HTTP 500 on a successful order.
defense_layers: PersistOrderCreatedToOutbox listener registered FIRST (EventServiceProvider:147) — outbox SSOT survives any peer listener throw
Inner StockService::mutateForOrder DB::transaction (StockService:49-51) — partial stock decrement rolls back atomically
DispatchableAfterCommit (Concerns/DispatchableAfterCommit.php:30-42) — events fire only after outer commit
attacks.test_evidence: No dedicated test asserts 'Decrement throws -> outbox row still exists'. Cross-validates with PK1-ARCH-01 (sibling zone) — listener-isolation policy not unified.
attacks.outcome: PARTIAL — outbox/KDS path survives (SSOT-first invariant honored), FCM kitchen push silently skipped on stock-listener crash, client receives 500 on a successful order.
attacks.residual_risk: P1 — cross-validates with WF4-ARCH-01 + PK1-ARCH-01. Recommend V1.0.2 unified failure-isolation across the 4 OrderCreated listeners.

attacks.expected_outcome: Resolver returns is_available=false reason='seasonal' (manual takes precedence over stock).
defense_layers: ChoiceAvailabilityResolver::availabilityFromLevel:281-284 — manual_unavailable_reason checked BEFORE on_hand
F-016a-BIS comment block (ChoiceAvailabilityResolver:276-280) — explicit reasoning preserved

StockService::isAutoStockRuptureReason :217-220 — distinguishes auto ('stock_rupture'/'out_of_stock') from manual (5 whitelisted values in StockLevel::MANUAL_UNAVAILABLE_REASONS:35-41) — auto-rupture decrement-driven flip never overrides manual
attacks.test_evidence: test_stock_zero_does_not_override_manual_admin_rupture_reason (StockRuptureAvailabilitySyncTest, passing per filter run). Plus the 3 ChoiceAvailabilityResolver* tests covering ingredient_rupture + stock_rupture priority.

attacks.expected_outcome: DB level allows negative on_hand because no CHECK constraint exists in migration 2026_04_27_143120.
defense_layers: StockLevel::booted() saving() throws InvalidArgumentException for on_hand<0 (StockLevel:66-74) — Eloquent only

No production code path issues raw stock_levels writes — all paths through StockService or AvailabilityService Eloquent layer
attacks.test_evidence: StockLevelSchemaTest::test_stock_level_rejects_reserved_greater_than_on_hand passes — Eloquent layer. NO test exercises raw DB::table('stock_levels')->update(['on_hand' => -1]).

attacks.residual_risk: P2 — cross-validates with WF4-DBA-02. Add CHECK constraints in V1.0.2 migration. Today's surface = 0 production callers.

attacks.vector: Cross-branch decrement leak — operator at branch 5 submits order with item_id=42 (catalog row but stock_levels row only exists for branch 3)
attacks.expected_outcome: Decrement should silently skip (no level for branch 5) — order succeeds without phantom stock mutation in branch 3.
defense_layers: StockService::mutateForOrderInTransaction:87-94 — StockLevel::query()->where('branch_id', $branchId)->where(stockable_type)->where(stockable_id) — explicit branch_id filter
BranchScope on StockLevel/StockMovement (StockLevel:25, StockMovement:23) — global scope filter, admin bypass
Pre-decrement: AvailabilityService::assertItemsOrderableForBranch — catalog check independent of stock_levels
attacks.test_evidence: test_branch_option_restricts_scope (StockScanRuptureCommandTest, passing) + implicit branch isolation across the 79 passing Stock tests (each fixture creates Branch + StockLevel scoped to that branch).
attacks.outcome: DEFEATED — explicit branch_id filter + BranchScope dual defense.

attacks.vector: Composition snapshot addon swap — attacker mutates composition_snapshot.addons[].addon_item_id between order create and refund, attempting to credit stock on the wrong addon
attacks.expected_outcome: Refund credits the original item (per the persisted composition_snapshot at decrement time) — frontend mutation has no leverage post-create.
defense_layers: composition_snapshot is JSON frozen at order creation (NF525 invariant per CLAUDE.md §8 Pricing SSOT)
StockService::decodeSnapshotAddons :317-322 — reads addons from persisted JSON, not from request
Refund release re-reads OrderItem from DB (StockService:364-367) — server-side trust
attacks.test_evidence: test_decrement_and_partial_refund_track_addon_target_stock_from_composition_snapshot (StockReleaseOnRefundTest:49-121) — addon stock decremented via composition_snapshot.addon_item_id, refunded back via the SAME snapshot; no client-controlled mutation surface.

findings.title: After-commit listener failure isolation policy not unified across the 4 OrderCreated listeners — cross-validates WF4-ARCH-01 and sibling PK1-ARCH-01
findings.evidence_read: After F-6 (5bb8c48f9) the StockUnavailableException catch is correct — but the Throwable branch still re-throws in an after-commit context. Sibling listener DecrementItemAvailabilityOnOrder has no try/catch (raw throw). SendFcmOnOrderCreated already isolates failure (try/catch). PersistOrderCreatedToOutbox catches DispatchDomainEventsJob::dispatch (PersistOrderCreatedToOutbox:67-78 — best-effort broadcast).
findings.impact: Mixed-policy = unpredictable behavior. Cross-validates with PK1-ARCH-01 from sibling PK-1-DATA-FLOW STATUS round-1 (intersection-pos-kds-2026-05-18). Owner sees 500 on successful order if either DecrementStockOnOrderCreated OR DecrementItemAvailabilityOnOrder throws unexpected.
findings.recommendation: V1.0.2 — wrap both decrement listeners with try/catch + SyncMetricsRecorder->recordDecrementFailure + return (do not re-throw). Order is already committed; the metric captures forensic visibility without HTTP-error-on-success UX. Keep PersistOrderCreatedToOutbox as the throw-on-failure SSOT.

findings.title: Trigger absence-of-defense test missing — empirical raw-query trigger fire untested
findings.evidence_read: Three test methods cover Eloquent update/delete LogicException + UNIQUE constraint. None exercise raw DB::table('stock_movements')->delete()/->update() to assert SQLite RAISE(ABORT) or MySQL SQLSTATE 45000.
findings.impact: Cross-validates WF4-DBA-01. If a future refactor accidentally drops the Eloquent boot guards, neither the unit tests nor the trigger migration's presence-on-disk catches the regression.
findings.recommendation: Add 2 test methods (~20 lines) — test_raw_delete_blocked_by_db_trigger + test_raw_update_blocked_by_db_trigger.
findings.scope_minimal_fix: HEAL-NOW candidate (clean file, no frozen-zone touch, ~20 lines). Defer to WF-7 RED-META synthesis decision.

findings.title: ChoiceAvailability resolver snapshot vs assert-orderable have subtly different parameters — snapshotForItems doesn't accept useRowLock, while assertSelectionsOrderable does
findings.evidence_read: snapshotForItems (read-path for POS/Kiosk filters) always uses useRowLock=false (ChoiceAvailabilityResolver:51 — stockLevelsForBranch:215 receives constant false). assertSelectionsOrderable accepts useRowLock as a parameter — true on order submit (Z5 SSOT scope), false on pricing preview.
findings.impact: VERY LOW — read-path is intentionally lockless (snapshot for menu display doesn't need to serialize with order commit). The asymmetry is by design. Risk: a future contributor adding a snapshot-then-decrement pattern in a single transaction might assume the snapshot locked rows — and it doesn't. Document the divergence explicitly.
findings.recommendation: Docblock-only — add to ChoiceAvailabilityResolver::snapshotForItems a note 'No row lock acquired; intended for read-path display only. For order-submit gates use assertSelectionsOrderable(useRowLock=true).'

findings.title: Listener throw inside `releaseForOrderInTransaction` ($order not Order/FrontendOrder type) silently no-ops
findings.evidence_read: StockService:62-64 — early return if $order instanceof Order && ! $order instanceof FrontendOrder. The 3 release-listener paths instantiate via OrderCanceled / RefundCreated — both events carry $order property which is Order|FrontendOrder. A future event type or test fixture passing a different Model bypass-silent no-ops.
findings.impact: VERY LOW — type-safe contract upstream. Risk = absence of warning if a contributor wires a new event type to StockService::releaseForOrder.
findings.recommendation: Log::warning + recordMetric on the early return path so silent no-ops become visible. Defer V1.0.2.

Refund release ledger via OrderItem.released_qty cap. Validated by partial-refund test sentinel.
ChoiceAvailability 5-layer precedence — manual > stock, catalog_inactive top of priority chain. Validated by 3 ChoiceAvailabilityResolver* test files.
Pre-decrement assertItemsOrderableForBranch + assertSelectionsOrderable chokepoint — soft-deleted Item / catalog_inactive / surface_hidden caught before stock mutation.
Composition_snapshot SSOT for addon stock — frozen JSON survives client-side mutation attempts. Validated by addon-refund test.
Outbox SSOT-first listener registration — stock-listener throw doesn't kill KDS push path.
Foundation F-6 P0-ARCH-01 + P0-DBA-01 dual fix — exception class path corrected + trigger defense layer added. Both verified applied via migrate:status + 79/79 Stock test pass.
BranchScope global scope on StockLevel + StockMovement — cross-tenant decrement leak defeated.
